internal_alignment: Parts of an analog clock (face, 12 numbers, short hour hand, long minute hand, center dot); reading hours (long hand on 12, short hand on the hour); reading half hours (long hand on 6, short hand halfway between two hour numbers); writing digital times in hours and half hours; drawing hands from a digital time; matching analog and digital times. Internal record only; no separate answer key is published for this pack.
model_accuracy: Every clock verified before rendering: only :00 and :30 times appear anywhere in the pack (26 clocks). Minute hand at 12 for every :00 and at 6 for every :30; hour hand exactly on the hour number for :00 and halfway between the hour numbers for :30 (30 degrees per hour plus 15 degrees at half past). Worked examples color-code the hands (teal hour, coral minute); practice clocks use navy hands distinguished by length alone. Page 1 answers: coloring short hands point to the 4, between the 10 and the 11, and to the 1; check short hands point to the 8 and between the 9 and the 10. Page 2: 5:00, 9:00, 12:00, 7:00 (12:00 hands overlap, short hand visible as the thicker base). Page 3 matches: 4:30, 8:30, 11:30, 2:30; 9:00 is the spare digital time. Page 4: 4:00, 10:00, 1:30, 9:30 with half-past short hands halfway between numbers. Page 5: 8:00 middle clock, 5:30 right clock, 12:30 left clock; each distractor differs in exactly one hand.
